title: Deadenylation and decapping factors cooperatively stimulate biochemical activities of DEAD-box ATPase Dhh1.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Pulled the Zenodo record via its API (record 21345236, CC-BY-4.0): 51 files, 908 MB total. Downloaded and read five of the small CSVs. 'ATP binding.csv' has 9 data rows (a 2-fold dilution series, 3 replicates, 2 conditions); 'FP_Dhh1_nucleotides.csv' has 11 rows x 5 nucleotide conditions x 3 replicates; 'FP_Edc3_constructs.csv' has 16 rows x 8 Edc3 variants x 3 replicates, with many blank cells; 'Sequence_conservation_Edc3.csv' is a 455-position ConSurf conservation table for one protein. Listed sizes/formats of everything else.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The derived numbers that the paper reports (dissociation constants, ATP-hydrolysis rate constants, the 200-fold cooperative stimulation) are in the article's figures and tables; I read the abstract and methods for them. I did not open the 31-66 MB proprietary Refeyn mass-photometry .mpr files or the 31 MB thin-layer-chromatography gel .tif images, only their listings.

a1_downloadable.note: Zenodo deposit is open, CC-BY-4.0, no login. I downloaded five files successfully.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. Nothing in the deposit is a fitted quantity. The CSVs hold raw instrument readings (fluorescence-polarisation millipolarisation units, raw scintillation counts) laid out as a titration grid with merged header cells; every binding constant or rate would have to be constructed by fitting a binding curve per condition and then hand-transcribing the paper's figure panels.

a3_inputs_present.note: Protein construct boundaries and mutations are in Supplementary Table S1 and AlphaFold3 structures are deposited, so inputs could be assembled — but there are only ~12 distinct protein variants.

a4_units_stated.note: Column headers give concentrations in micromolar; fluorescence polarisation is in millipolarisation units. Units are stated for what is there.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL, decisively. Counted in the files: roughly 12 distinct protein variants/complexes, each measured as an 8-16 point titration in triplicate. That is of order 10^1 labelled examples where the checklist needs ~1,500 (or ~400 for classification). The 908 MB is raw instrument output for a dozen experiments, not a dozen thousand measurements.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: under 5 MB of CSV; the rest is raw gel images and proprietary binary
a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially fits, which is cold comfort given there is nothing to fit.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The file names map cleanly onto the paper's figure panels; no conflicting counts, because no counts are claimed.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels would come from real biochemistry (radiolabelled ATP hydrolysis assays, fluorescence polarisation, mass photometry), not from another model's output. Provenance is clean; there is simply far too little of it.

honest_claim_h3: No model is supportable: with roughly a dozen measured protein variants, any claim would be a curve fit with a confidence interval, not a prediction.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use protein partner and mutation identity to predict how much a helper protein speeds up an RNA-decay enzyme.
plain_idea.train_on: What I considered: one row per protein complex (the enzyme Dhh1 plus a partner protein or a mutated partner), described by sequence and predicted structure. I counted only about 12 such complexes in the deposited files.
plain_idea.predict: The enzyme's ATP-hydrolysis rate or its binding strength for ATP and RNA, measured in the lab by radiolabelled-ATP assays and fluorescence polarisation (a method that reports binding by how slowly a labelled molecule tumbles).
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: If it worked it would tell RNA-decay labs which partner-protein contacts to mutate next, but at a dozen examples the data cannot support a model; it is a hypothesis-generating biochemistry paper, not a training set.

ml_idea: None viable. The only machine-learning-shaped framing — predict ATPase stimulation or binding affinity from the identity of the partner protein and its mutations — has about 12 examples. The adjacent, well-populated version of this task (predicting how mutations change protein-protein binding) is already served by public resources such as SKEMPI and by several 2021-2025 models (Pythia-PPI, DeepPPAPredMut and others found in search), none of which this deposit would meaningfully extend.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the actual file sizes I downloaded; no timing was needed because the usable tabular data is under 5 MB.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the distinct protein variants in the deposited CSV headers. I did: about 12. That alone ends it, and it took one download.

verdict_reason: Fails A5 and A2: a dozen protein variants measured as raw titration curves, with every rate and binding constant still to be fitted.
